column1: # Elevation-Storage Curves for Reservoirs
# Some data sources report water surface elevation rather than storage volume.
# This file contains the lookup tables to convert elevation (ft) to storage (af).
# Format: location_id
# - Each location_id can have multiple rows defining the curve
# - Elevations should be in ascending order
# - Linear interpolation is used between points
# Sources:
# - 11507001 (Upper Klamath Lake): 2017 revision of UKL elevation-capacity curve
#   from KBAO Hydro Team (Daily_UKL_net_inflow_Apr2017_FINAL)
#   Units: elevation = ft BOR datum
#   Table includes present configuration with northern marshes and Tulana Farms/Goose Bay
# - 10337000 (Lake Tahoe A Tahoe City CA): elevation-capacity curve from Gregg
#   Reynolds / Lahontan Basin Area Office (LBAO)
#   IMPORTANT: Tahoe rows are indexed by USGS gage height
#   (= lake_surface_elev_LTD - 6220.00 ft)
#   The USGS gage datum at Lake Tahoe sits at 6220.00 ft LTD
#   BELOW the natural rim of Lake Tahoe (6223.00 ft LTD). Therefore:
#     gage_height = 0.0  -> lake surface at 6220.00 LTD (well below rim)
#     gage_height = 3.0  -> lake surface at 6223.00 LTD (natural rim
#     gage_height = 9.1  -> lake surface at 6229.10 LTD (legal max
#     gage_height = 9.5  -> lake surface at 6229.50 LTD (curve max
#   Storage at and below the natural rim is clamped to 0 acre-feet.
#   Range: gage_height -1.00 to +9.50 ft
#   Units: elevation_ft = gage_height ft above local gage datum
location_id
